## Cycle 135 — 2026-10-22 — pre-registration (written BEFORE the cycle's first repair and before the first artifact write beyond this block)

Cycle 135 executes the Cycle-134 handoff's three priorities. This block is the pre-registration. The seven
audit checks and their decision rules, the repair list with its before/after, and the decision procedure for
the register's own structural question are all fixed here, so that neither a repair nor a verdict can be
re-written after the fact.

### Three-pass task-framing loop

**Pass 1 — Draft.** Objective: **(Priority 1)** audit the completed backward state inventory *as a whole* —
it is the register's largest single artifact, it was completed in one sitting, and it has never been audited
as a whole — under seven pre-registered checks, and repair any record defect found in place; **(Priority 2)**
write the register's own structural question down exactly — the dependency between the narrowed rule, the
coverage map and the literature — decide whether the method is total or has a legitimate exit, and either
specify the exit within the standing rules or record a bounded, honest negative; **(Priority 3)** track the
open gaps (**no action on G-37, no action on G-33**) and run housekeeping. Scope boundary: theory only; **zero
fetches**; no market-data acquisition or processing; no computation of any strategy statistic; no backtest,
simulation, parameter sweep or significance test; no strategy or signal implementation; no executable research
infrastructure; no job or workflow launch; no change to the canonical prompt; no trading.

**Pass 2 — Critique.** (i) *An audit that can fit its repairs is not an audit.* The seven checks and their
decision rules are fixed **in this block, before the first repair**; the repair list is fixed **in this block,
before the first repair**. (ii) *An audit must not become a re-run of the route it audits.* The backward route
is exhausted and is **not** re-run: the audit reads the register's own tables **as tables** and checks their
internal arithmetic, agreement and resolution. **No source is re-read, no `S-` identifier is consumed, and no
document is fetched.** (iii) *A repair must not change a finding.* Every repair is a **record** repair. **No
score, rank, hard-stop flag, gap status, rejection verdict or candidate status may move**, and no map row or
baseline row may be added, removed or renumbered. (iv) *Priority 2 must not become a literature licence by the
back door.* The **Cycle-132 rejection of the literature-first route amendment is the standing precedent**; any
exit specified must respect it; **no candidate may be created unless a construction survives the screens**; and
**any kill must name its clause**. (v) *The audit's own limits must be stated, not assumed.* The corpus is a
corpus of literature the register chose to read; the map remains a **lower bound**; and an audit of the
register's own tables can establish the register's *internal* consistency but can never establish that the
register's prior art is complete. (vi) *The audit must test its own premises.* Two of the seven checks as
worded in the handoff carry premises that may be false; the check must report the premise as well as the
verdict, and a false premise is a finding about the check, not a failure of the artifact.

**Pass 3 — Revise and red-team (the task as executed).** Record: the seven checks with their verdicts and
their evidence; the repair list with a before/after for each repair; the register's own structural question
stated formally, with the totality question decided and the exit either specified within the standing rules or
recorded as a bounded negative; the open gaps tracked; the counts re-derived from the files; the rubric
arithmetic re-run; all five artifact headers and their newest dated blocks advanced to "Cycle 135 complete"
and **read back in this session**; the standing identifier-integrity check run. Every external claim points to
an `S-` entry. **No `IDEA-` identifier may be consumed unless a blind construction is written before any
literature is read.**

### Priority 1 — the closure audit of the completed inventory. REGISTERED BEFORE THE FIRST REPAIR.

**The instrument, and the order.** The instrument is **the register's own artifacts**: `rejected_and_parked.md`
(the inventory tables, the coverage map, the rejection log), `source_ledger.md` (the corpus), `idea_register.md`
(the gap ledger). **Zero fetches.** The checks are run **one at a time**, in the order (a) … (g), and each
verdict is recorded before the next check is run.

**The seven checks, with their decision rules fixed in advance.**

- **(a) Identifier partition.** *PASS* if the union of the inventory tables' identifier sets equals the ledger's
  entry-block identifier set **exactly**, with **no gap**, **no identifier outside the corpus**, and **no
  identifier appearing in two different batch tables**. The corpus is the set of `### S-NNN` headings in
  `source_ledger.md` **plus** the ten Cycle-58 document-record entries S-281 … S-290, which carry no heading of
  their own; the only reserved-and-unused range is S-210 … S-219. *FAIL* otherwise.
- **(b) Cell-vs-tally agreement.** *PASS* if every recorded **batch outcome line** equals the tally of that
  batch's **own cells**, the cells being the primary record and each cell being classified by its own recorded
  in/out-of-map verdict. *FAIL* otherwise, and the outcome line is corrected to the cells' tally with the
  disagreement recorded in place.
- **(c) Map resolution.** *PASS* if every coverage-map row **named** in an in-map cell **exists** in the map
  (A–I, 10–33) and if every row of the map **names the closing entry** that closes it. **Recorded separately,
  not as a pass/fail:** the number of in-map cells that **name no map row** (their resolution is then by
  family, in the "already claimed?" column), because the map's rows and the known-baseline table's rows are two
  different numberings and a cell may legitimately cite either.
- **(d) Kill resolution.** *PASS* if every cell whose verdict is out-of-map names a kill **by clause or
  template** and is mapped — at the level of the entry that records the kill — to a coverage-map row and a
  known-baseline row, and if **no out-of-map entry stands without both a kill and a mapping**. *FAIL*
  otherwise.
- **(e) Disagreement completeness.** *PASS* if every (iv-b) entry that is a **disagreement** records **both**
  readings, names the **stricter** one adopted and **states why**. **The count of (iv-b) entries that are not
  disagreements at all is reported explicitly**, so that the check's own premise — that all four are
  disagreements — is tested rather than assumed.
- **(f) Whole-corpus arithmetic.** *PASS* if the **272 in-map · 172 not-a-state (168 (iv-a), 4 (iv-b)) · 3
  out-of-map** distribution and the **447** total are re-derived **from the cells** and equal the recorded
  figures. *FAIL* otherwise.
- **(g) Gap-ledger completeness.** *PASS* if every `G-` identifier consumed in any cycle is recorded in
  `idea_register.md` **with its status**, or is explicitly listed among the identifiers absent from the
  register **with a reason**. The specific item the Cycle-134 identifier-integrity check flagged — **G-31** — is
  the one to resolve: its status is confirmed from `cycle_notes.md` and written into the register.

**The repair list. REGISTERED BEFORE THE FIRST REPAIR.** Every item is a record repair. Each is stated with
its before and after. **No other repair is permitted**, and in particular **no cell is re-classified, no map row
or baseline row is added, removed or renumbered, and no figure outside the two lines named below changes.**

1. **Any batch outcome line that disagrees with its own cells is corrected to the cells' tally, with the
   disagreement and its resolution recorded in the same place.** The cells are the primary record.
2. **Any sentence in an entry that states a count its own table contradicts is corrected in place, with the
   before/after recorded.**
3. **G-31 is written into `idea_register.md`** with its confirmed status and its provenance, in IDEA-010's
   dossier, where G-30's exhaustion is already recorded, so that the gap-ledger position is legible to a later
   session without a cross-file inference.
4. **Nothing else.** A repair that would alter a score, a rank, a hard-stop flag, a gap's status, a rejection's
   verdict, a candidate's status, a map row, a baseline row or a classification is **not** a repair and is
   **not** made.

### Priority 2 — the register's own structural question, stated and decided. REGISTERED BEFORE THE ANALYSIS IS WRITTEN.

**The question.** The Cycle-134 handoff states the register's difficulty as a **dependency loop in its own
method**: the narrowed rule forbids the literature until a construction passes screens that are themselves built
from the map, while the map can only be extended by the literature. Cycle 135's task is to write that loop
down exactly and decide it.

**The procedure, fixed in advance.** (i) **State it formally** — name the objects (the recorded prior art, the
screen, the construction, the literature), state what the narrowed rule permits and forbids, and identify the
precise point at which the dependency closes on itself. (ii) **Test totality** — ask whether the method is
*closed under its own screens* (every construction it can supply receives a verdict and the productive range is
non-empty) or whether it has a legitimate exit, and answer the question with the register's own numbers rather
than with an argument. (iii) **If it has an exit**, specify it in a form that respects the standing rules: a
**named clause**, a **bounded scope**, **zero fetches until a construction survives the screens**, and an
**explicit licence-and-enforcement bound**, with the **Cycle-132 rejection of the literature-first route
amendment as the standing precedent** that any specification must answer and not re-propose. (iv) **If it has
no exit**, say so plainly and record the register's position as a **bounded, honest negative** with the numbers
attached: **33 map rows; 447 of 447 corpus entries probed from the other side; zero out-of-map survivors; fifteen
named constructions, all killed.**

**The pre-registered constraints on the answer.** (a) **No candidate is created** unless a construction survives
the screens, and any kill must name its clause. (b) **No route is re-run**: not the backward route (exhausted),
not G-37's bounded search, not G-33's dated routes, and **not the Cycle-132 literature-first route amendment** —
a re-specification may be *drafted*, but a drafted clause is neither executed nor adopted, and a draft is not a
candidate. (c) **The answer must distinguish the method's *epistemic* limit from the register's *empirical*
emptiness**, because the handoff's framing may conflate them, and the audit's job is to say which is which.
(d) The analysis is of the register's **own artifacts**, not a literature route.

## Cycle 135 — Priority 2 — the register's own structural question, stated and decided

**No `R-` identifier is consumed by this priority, and no gap is opened.** This is not a kill of a construction —
nothing was screened — so there is no verdict to record in the rejection log. It is a statement about the
register's *method*, and it is recorded here, in the file where the register's one other method-level document
(the Cycle-131 literature-first draft) lives.

### The question, stated exactly

The Cycle-134 handoff stated the register's difficulty as **a dependency loop in its own method**: *"the narrowed
rule forbids the literature until a construction passes screens that are themselves built from the map, while the
map can only be extended by the literature."* The task is to write that loop down precisely, decide whether the
method is **total** or has a **legitimate exit**, and either specify the exit within the standing rules or record
a bounded, honest negative with the numbers attached.

### The formal statement

**Objects.**
- **P** — the register's **recorded prior art**: the coverage map **M** (33 rows: A–I, 10–33) ∪ the
  known-baseline table **B** (111 rows) ∪ the nine state-kind and constraint templates **T** (A–I) ∪ the
  sixty-eight rejection verdicts.
- **A** — the **narrowed rule** (R-063's, unchanged since Cycle 117), a *function of P*: **(i)** the constructed
  state must not be an accounting by-product of the flow it would trade; **(ii)** the constructed price wedge must
  not already be in **B**; **(iii)** **T** must be run against the construction *before the literature*; plus the
  strict bar — a **published decision-time state**, **sign-determining** rather than magnitude, an **unclaimed
  sign**, a **feasible clean test** — plus the **Cycle-52 third test** (the state must not be a public real-time
  by-product of the flow).
- **C** — a **construction** = (state, flow, sign claim, instance).
- **L** — the **external published literature**.

**The register's method, M_reg.** *Supply* a construction **C**; apply **A(C)**; if **A** kills **C**, record the
kill and add the kind to **M** and **B**; if **A** survives **C**, then **L** becomes reachable for **C** — the
rule's own words, as R-064 restates them: *"Under rule (iii) the literature is reached only by a survivor"* — and
**L** is then used to locate an instance and to check that the price wedge is unclaimed; if it is unclaimed, **C**
becomes a candidate.

**Where the dependency closes.** **L ← A ← P ← L**, in three steps:
1. **A is a function of P.** Every clause of the screen appeals to something P records — a baseline row, a
   template, a recorded kill.
2. **P is a function of L.** The map's rows and the baseline table's rows are, apart from the constructions the
   register wrote from its own knowledge, entries L supplied.
3. **L is reachable only from a survivor of A.**
⇒ **P can only grow through L; L can only be reached through A; A is a function of P.** The loop is closed, and it
closes in exactly one place: **A's own adequacy cannot be tested by A.**

### The decisive separation: two different limits, and the handoff's framing conflates them

**(i) The epistemic closure — real, and irreducible.** Because the only instrument that can reach a state kind
outside **M** is **L**, and **L** is gated behind a survivor produced by **A**, the register cannot in principle
use its own screens to discover its own blind spot. This is not a defect in the method; it is the ordinary
condition of any screening method whose screen derives from a finite record. **The correct response to it is a
stated bound, not a licence** — and the register has already stated the bound correctly, in R-064 (*"the map is
the register's lower bound on the space, not a proof of exhaustiveness"*), in R-067, and in R-068 (*"the corpus is
a corpus of literature the register chose to read … the register has no instrument that makes it one"*).

**(ii) The empirical emptiness of the productive range — real, but NOT caused by the loop.** If the loop were the
binding constraint it would forbid *new* state kinds. **It does not.** The map grew from **21 rows** (R-064) to
**24** (R-066) to **28** (R-067) to **33** (R-068 and the Cycle-131 additions) **because of** the constructions,
each of which produced a new kind *and* a named kill. Fifteen named constructions across R-063 … R-068 (R-063 1,
R-064 3, R-065 1, R-066 3, R-067 4, R-068 3 out-of-map kinds plus the closure of set (3)), plus the Cycles
115–121 state-kind screens, **not one has produced a candidate** — R-068's own count, which Cycle 135 adopts
unchanged. Every one was killed **at the design stage, at a cost of zero fetches**, by a **named clause**: the
accounting-by-product clause, the obligor's-own-flow clause, the sign-versus-magnitude clause, the
published-baseline clause, a template match, or the count-dilemma.

**So the dependency is real; it is not what stopped a candidate. What stopped a candidate is that every
construction the register has been able to write was killed on its own merits.**

### Is the method total?

A method is **total** over its input domain if it returns a verdict for every input, and **productive** if the
candidate branch is non-empty on the domain it actually faces.

- **Total: yes.** Every construction the register has supplied received a verdict, every verdict was a kill naming
  a clause or a template, and **zero constructions were left undecided**. The screen is decision-complete: it
  always decides.
- **Productive: no.** The candidate branch is **empty over fifteen named constructions** and, since Cycle 134, the
  register's second supply route is closed: the backward route has read **447 of 447** corpus entries (**100 %**,
  at a cost of zero fetches) and returned **272 in-map · 172 not-a-state (168 (iv-a), 4 (iv-b)) · 3 out-of-map
  entries, all three killed and mapped · 0 out-of-map survivors**.

**The accurate verdict: the method is total and empty.** It decides every input it is given and has never
converted an input into a candidate. It is a **screening** method, not a **generating** method, and it is closed
under its own screens and open at exactly **one** place: **it requires an input to be supplied.**

### The exit

The formal analysis delivers something the handoff's framing did not anticipate. **The exit is not a licence to
read literature. It is a third source of constructions.** The register has used exactly two supply routes, and
both are now closed or exhausted:

1. **The forward route** — constructions written from the register's own knowledge of mechanisms, screened blind.
   **Fifteen constructions, every one killed by a named clause, zero fetches.** R-068's own diagnosis is exact:
   the map is made of the same memory the constructions are drawn from, so a construction is guaranteed to be
   screened against a map built from itself. The space of mechanisms is not finite, but the register's *own
   memory* is the only supply it has used, and it has drawn on that supply fifteen times without a survivor.
2. **The backward route** — read the register's own corpus for the state each published price effect conditions
   on. **Exhausted at Cycle 134** (447 of 447; zero out-of-map survivors), and it is closed as a route in any case:
   it supplies *states*, not constructions, and it can only supply states the register has already read.

**The exit is therefore a route that supplies constructions from neither source** — and there is exactly one such
route available inside the register's own artifacts at zero cost: **the map itself.**

### Clause X-1 — the near-miss probe. DRAFTED, NOT ADOPTED, NOT EXECUTED.

- **What it is.** For each **closed** coverage-map row, the register names the **nearest state kind that the
  row's own closing clause does not cover**, writes it as a construction (state, flow, sign claim, instance), and
  screens it under the **unchanged** narrowed rule. The **map's rows are the source of the constructions** — not
  the register's free memory, and not the literature. That is precisely what separates X-1 from the forward
  family screens, and it is why X-1 is not a re-run of any exhausted route.
- **The precedent it generalises is the register's own.** R-067 carried a residual forward because *"a kill which
  cannot name a clause is not a kill"*, and R-068 ran **D4** — a named rescuing sub-variant of a closed kind — and
  killed it by the **count-dilemma**, closing **row 27 in full**. **The register has run this probe once, in one
  of thirty-three rows, and it worked as a method**: it converted "closed as a kind" into "closed in full".
- **What it does not change.** Clauses (i), (ii), the strict bar, the Cycle-52 third test and the nine templates
  are **unchanged**. The rediscovery guard is **unchanged**: a killed probe's kind is added to the map and to the
  baseline table with its kill; a surviving probe is a **construction**, not yet a candidate.
- **Bounded scope.** **The 33 map rows**, at most **one probe per row**, written **blind** — that is, before the
  row's closing clause is re-read — so that a probe is not simply the negation of the kill it is testing. Rows
  are taken in pre-registered batches: **A–I** (the template programme), **10–17**, **18–25**, **26–33**. If the
  next cycle's budget is short, **one batch of eight** may be run and the remainder deferred; the batch boundary
  is fixed in advance, by row, so that the choice of which rows to probe cannot be made after seeing a result.
- **Zero fetches until a construction survives the screens.** The probe reads **no document**. **X-1 does not
  consult the literature at all**, so it is not the literature-first route and does not re-open the Cycle-132
  decision. If a probe **survives** the screen, the narrowed rule's **own** exit opens — the literature becomes
  reachable **for that construction alone**, and that is the only circumstance in which this method spends a
  fetch.
- **Enforcement bound.** A killed probe is killed by a **named clause**, as always, and the kill is written into
  the map row and the baseline table. There is **no partial survivor**: a probe survives only by satisfying every
  clause. A surviving probe must then pass the rule's literature step before it can become a candidate.
- **The honest prior, stated in advance.** **R-068's D4 found a sub-variant and killed it.** One probe in one row
  produced a kill, and that is the register's **entire** evidence base for X-1. **X-1 is not expected to produce a
  candidate.** It is expected to produce either a kill with a named clause — the common case, and a genuine gain,
  because it closes a row *in full* rather than by kind — or a survivor, which opens the register's own exit.
  Either outcome is a gain in the register's knowledge; **neither is a candidate.**
- **Relation to the Cycle-132 rejection — the standing precedent, respected.** The Cycle-132 decision rejected
  the *literature-first route amendment* because (a) the "disinterested publisher" clause is not operational on
  the aggregated-obligor side, and (b) a ten-document budget creates scope-creep pressure, with the empirical
  premise that the backward route was still running and was the better thing to continue. **X-1 answers neither
  question by re-proposing the route; it is a different route that reads no literature and consults no external
  source.** For the record, **reason (b)'s empirical premise is now spent** — the backward route was carried to
  completion (Cycle 134, 447 of 447) — and **reason (a) stands untouched**. **X-1 does not re-open the Cycle-132
  decision, and this cycle does not re-open it either.**
- **The decision not to execute X-1 in Cycle 135, recorded with its reason.** X-1 is a **route**, and a route
  requires its own pre-registration, its own batch boundaries and its own outcome categories, in a cycle that has
  time to run them. Executing it in the same cycle that specified it would make the specification unfalsifiable
  by construction, and would spend the register's one clean cycle on a route whose own prior is one probe in one
  row. **It is therefore handed to Cycle 136 as Priority 1, to be pre-registered there before its first probe is
  written.** The handoff's own constraint is respected: **this task creates no candidate**, because no
  construction has survived and none was screened.

### One further finding, about the register's own rule rather than about the world

**The narrowed rule is stricter than the mission it serves, and the register should know that.** The canonical
prompt's own CONTINUOUS RESEARCH LOOP places **"Seek credible sources" (step 3) before "Form candidate hypotheses"
(step 4)**, and defines originality as differentiation from *"the ideas already in this repository **and the
closest known public analogues**"* — i.e. the mission expects the literature to be read as a matter of course, and
expects prior art to be checked against published work rather than only against the register's own record. The
narrowed rule inverts that order for the *forward* route: it gates the literature behind a survivor. That
inversion is the register's **own** methodological choice, not a requirement of the canonical prompt, and the
canonical prompt is maintainer-owned and is **not** modified here. The finding is recorded because it bears
directly on the exit: **the loop is a self-imposed narrowing**, and X-1 is a way to reach an exit *without*
reversing it. Any future decision to reverse it would be a decision about the register's own method, and would
have to be taken against the Cycle-132 precedent rather than around it.

### The register's position after Priority 2 — the bounded, honest negative, with the numbers

1. **The method is total in form and empty in content on its actual input domain.** It has decided every
   construction it has been given — **fifteen named constructions across R-063 … R-068, plus the Cycles 115–121
   state-kind screens, all killed at the design stage at a cost of zero fetches** — and it has never produced a
   candidate.
2. **The dependency loop the handoff names is real, but it is the *epistemic* limit, not the cause of the
   emptiness.** The map grew 21 → 24 → 28 → 33 **because of** the constructions, and every kill was a named clause
   applied to a new kind.
3. **The binding constraint is the supply of constructions.** The register's two supply routes are closed or
   exhausted: its own memory (fifteen constructions, all killed) and its own corpus (**447 of 447**, zero
   out-of-map survivors).
4. **The exit is a supply route, and exactly one requires no licence and no fetch: X-1, the near-miss probe of
   the register's own map**, generalised from the one instance the register has already run and recorded
   (R-067's carried-forward residual → R-068's D4 → row 27 closed in full). It is **specified above, with a named
   clause, a bounded scope, zero fetches until a construction survives, and an explicit enforcement bound**, and
   it is **not executed in this cycle**.
5. **The register's own bound stands and is not moved:** **33 map rows · 447 of 447 corpus entries probed from the
   other side · zero out-of-map survivors · fifteen named constructions, all killed · 0 candidates · 0 fetches
   spent on the forward route.** The map remains a **lower bound** on the space of published state kinds, because
   the corpus is a corpus the register chose to read, and no instrument in the register makes it otherwise.

## Cycle 136 — 2026-10-22 — pre-registration (written BEFORE the cycle's first artifact write beyond this block, and BEFORE the first probe was written)

Cycle 136 executes the Cycle-135 handoff's three priorities. This block is the pre-registration. The batch of
probes, the blind-writing rule, the outcome categories and the stated expectation are fixed here for Priority 1;
the five audit checks, their decision rules and the repair list are fixed here for Priority 2; and the gap
tracking and the housekeeping list are fixed here for Priority 3 — so that neither a verdict, a repair nor a
count can be re-written after the fact.

### Three-pass task-framing loop

**Pass 1 — Draft.** Objective: **(Priority 1)** *execute* clause X-1, the near-miss probe of the register's own
coverage map, in **batch 1 (rows A–I)** — the nine template rows — writing each probe blind and screening it under
the **unchanged** narrowed rule; **(Priority 2)** audit the **known-baseline table** (111 rows) as a whole for the
first time, under five pre-registered checks, and repair any record defect in place; **(Priority 3)** track the
open gaps (**no action on G-37, no action on G-33**) and run housekeeping. Scope boundary: theory only; **zero
fetches** unless and until a probe survives the screens and the narrowed rule's own literature step is reached
(it is not expected to be); no market-data acquisition or processing; no computation of any strategy statistic; no
backtest, simulation, parameter sweep or significance test; no strategy or signal implementation; no executable
research infrastructure; no job or workflow launch; no change to the canonical prompt; no trading.

**Pass 2 — Critique.** (i) *A probe that is written after the kill it tests is a tautology.* The blind-writing
rule is fixed **in this block, before the first probe is written**, and the nine probes are written **as a block**,
**before** the batch's nine closing entries (`R-039 … R-046`) and the batch's nine known-baseline rows (68 … 75)
are read. (ii) *A probe must not become a re-run of a route the register has already closed.* X-1 reads **no
document**, consults **no literature**, and is not the forward route (constructions from the register's free
memory), not the backward route (447 of 447, exhausted) and not the Cycle-132 literature-first route amendment
(rejected, and **not** re-opened). Its **source of constructions is the map's own rows**, which is precisely what
separates it from the forward family screens. (iii) *A probe must not be a rediscovery.* If a probe reproduces a
construction the register has already screened (R-063 … R-068, or the Cycles 115–121 state-kind screens), the
outcome category is **REDISCOVERY**, recorded as such and **not** counted as a new kill — the batch would then
have been badly chosen, and that is recorded against the batch rather than against the register. (iv) *A kill must
name its clause.* As in every previous construction-first screen, a probe that dies dies **by a named clause or
template**, and a probe that cannot name one **is not killed** — it is recorded as **UNDECIDED** and handed off,
because the register's own principle ("a kill which cannot name a clause is not a kill") cuts both ways.
(v) *The expectation must be stated before the result and must not substitute for the screen.* The expectation
(nine kills) is recorded below and the screen is run regardless of it. (vi) *The audit must not become a re-run
of the route it audits.* Priority 2 audits the baseline table **as a table**; it re-reads no source and consumes no
`S-` identifier. (vii) *The audit must not become a licence.* A row that cannot be sourced is **marked**, not
silently deleted, and the rediscovery guard is not weakened by any repair.

**Pass 3 — Revise and red-team (the task as executed).** Record: the nine probes as written blind; the nine
screens with their named clause or template; the batch's outcome tally; the map and baseline edits the batch
requires; the five audit checks with their verdicts and their evidence; the repair list with a before/after for
each repair; the open gaps tracked; the counts re-derived **from the files**; the rubric arithmetic re-run **from
the shortlist's own cells**; all five artifact headers and their newest dated blocks advanced to "Cycle 136
complete" and **read back in this session**; the standing identifier-integrity check run. Every external claim
points to an `S-` entry. **No `IDEA-` identifier may be consumed unless a probe survives every screen *and* then
passes the narrowed rule's own literature step.**

### Priority 1 — clause X-1, the near-miss probe, **batch 1: coverage-map rows A–I**. REGISTERED BEFORE THE FIRST PROBE WAS WRITTEN.

**The instrument.** The register's own artifacts: the coverage map (33 rows), the narrowed rule (R-063's, unchanged
since Cycle 117), the strict bar, the Cycle-52 third test, the nine templates, the known-baseline table and the
rejection log. **The probe reads no document and consults no literature.** **Zero fetches** unless a probe
survives and the rule's own literature step is then reached.

**The batch, fixed in advance: rows A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I** — the nine template-programme rows, in the map's own
order. **At most one probe per row.** The batch boundary is fixed **here**, before any probe is written, so that
the choice of which rows to probe cannot be made after seeing a result. (The remaining twenty-four rows —
10–17, 18–25, 26–33 — are **deferred**, not cancelled; they are the batches 2, 3 and 4 named in X-1's
specification.)

**The blind-writing rule, fixed in advance.** For each row in the batch, the probe is written from **the row's map
label alone** — the "Published state kind" cell, with its parenthetical examples where the map gives them —
together with the register's own method (the narrowed rule, the strict bar, G-12, G-13, the Cycle-52 third test,
and the nine templates as *labels*). The row's **closing rejection entry** and the row's **known-baseline row** are
**not read** until **all nine probes in the batch are written and fixed in this file**. Each probe is written with
the register's four fields — **state**, **flow**, **sign claim**, **instance** — and with an explicit statement of
**the one feature that differs from the row's own kind**, which is what makes it a *near-miss* rather than a
restatement of the kind.

**The four outcome categories, fixed in advance.**

1. **KILL — named clause or template.** The probe is killed by a **named** clause (the accounting-by-product
   clause; the obligor's-own-flow clause; the sign-versus-magnitude clause, **G-12**; the anticipation clause,
   **G-13**; the published-baseline clause, rule (ii); the Cycle-52 third test; the strict bar's decision-time and
   feasible-clean-test limbs) or by a **named template** (A–I) or by a **named structural result already recorded**
   (for example the **count-dilemma**, R-068 D4). The kill is written into the map row and the known-baseline
   table with the clause named.
2. **SURVIVOR.** The probe satisfies **every** clause of the narrowed rule. **There is no partial survivor.** A
   survivor is a **construction**, not a candidate: the narrowed rule's **own** literature step must then be run on
   it (and only then may it become a candidate). **This is the only circumstance in which this method spends a
   fetch**, and it is not expected to be reached.
3. **REDISCOVERY.** The probe reproduces a construction the register has already screened. It is recorded as
   rediscovery, it is **not** counted as a new kill, and the batch's selection is faulted.
4. **UNDECIDED.** The screen cannot return a verdict without a fetch that the rule does not license at this point.
   It is **recorded and handed off**, never dropped.

**The stated expectation, fixed in advance and not permitted to substitute for the screen: nine kills.** The
reason is the register's own: a sub-variant of a kind is usually covered by the clause that closed the kind, and
the register's **entire** prior evidence on X-1 is one probe in one row — R-067's carried-forward residual →
R-068's D4 → the count-dilemma → **row 27 closed in full** — which produced a kill. **A survivor is possible**
and would be the register's **first in fifteen constructions** and would open the narrowed rule's own exit.
**Either outcome is a gain**: a kill closes a row **in full** rather than by kind; a survivor is the only thing
that can open the exit. **Nine kills is the expectation, not the result.**

**What this priority may consume.** An **`R-` identifier** (a new rejection entry recording the batch's kills),
and **baseline rows** (a killed probe's kind is written into the map row and the known-baseline table, with its
kill — and, following R-068 D4's precedent, if the killed probe's kind is a **member** of the row's existing kind
rather than a new kind, the row is **amended in place** and **no new baseline row** is written, because a
duplicate guard row would be a false claim of novelty). An **`IDEA-` identifier only if** a probe survives every
screen **and** then passes the rule's own literature step. **No `S-` identifier** unless that literature step is
reached. **No `G-` identifier** is opened, because every kill is expected to be structural and independent of data
availability.

### Priority 2 — the closure audit of the known-baseline table (111 rows). REGISTERED BEFORE THE FIRST CHECK IS RUN.

**The instrument, and the order.** The instrument is **the register's own artifacts**: `rejected_and_parked.md` (the
known-baseline table, the coverage map, the rejection log), `source_ledger.md` (the corpus), `idea_register.md`
(the gap ledger). **Zero fetches.** The five checks are run **one at a time**, in the order (a) … (e), and each
verdict is recorded before the next check is run.

**The five checks, with their decision rules fixed in advance.**

- **(a) Sourcing.** *PASS* if every baseline row either **names a source or rejection identifier that exists** in
  the ledger or the rejection log, **or** is explicitly marked as a **family-level row** — a general,
  well-established family the register treats as a baseline without a single anchor source. The handoff records
  that **five rows currently name neither**; the check must identify them **by position**, decide for each
  whether it can be anchored to an existing `S-`/`R-` identifier **already in the register** (no new identifier may
  be minted for this) **or** must be marked as a family-level row, and record the decision for each.
- **(b) Map coverage.** *PASS* if (i) every number cited in a coverage-map row's "known-baseline rows" cell
  **exists** in the baseline table, **and** (ii) every baseline row is **cited by at least one** coverage-map row's
  "known-baseline rows" cell. The two directions are reported **separately**, because the register has confused
  the two numberings before. The table's numbering is **positional** (row 1 is the first data row after the
  header and separator), which the check must state and verify.
- **(c) No duplication.** *PASS* if no two baseline rows describe the same family. A row that is a **variant** of
  another row is a duplication unless the pair states the difference explicitly.
- **(d) Numbering integrity.** *PASS* if the table is a **single contiguous block** (no stray blank line or
  non-row line splitting it — the defect class Cycle 109 repaired), if its positional numbering is **unambiguous**,
  if every row is **reachable** (counted and locatable), and if no row is **orphaned** (in the table but cited by
  nothing and naming nothing). Every map citation of the form "row N" must resolve to the family the map claims
  it names, for the cited rows that the check samples in full.
- **(e) In-place amendments.** *PASS* if every row amended in place carries its **amendment annotation**. The
  handoff names **rows 38, 44, 52 and 105**; the check must find **every** amended row, not only those, and
  record the ones it finds in addition.

**The repair list. REGISTERED BEFORE THE FIRST REPAIR.** Every item is a **record** repair, made **in place**,
with a **before and after**.

1. **Sourcing defects** — a row that names an identifier that does **not** exist is corrected to the identifier
   that does, or marked as a family-level row; a row that names nothing is marked as a family-level row, with the
   reason recorded.
2. **Map-citation defects** — a map row's citation of a baseline number that does not exist is corrected to the
   number that does; a baseline row that no map row cites is **not** deleted and **not** renumbered: the map is
   amended to cite it, or the row is recorded as **not represented in the map**, with the reason.
3. **Duplication defects** — recorded; **no row is deleted**. Where two rows describe one family, the later row
   is annotated as a **variant** of the earlier and the pair is cross-linked.
4. **Numbering-integrity defects** — a stray blank line or a non-row line inside the table is removed, with the
   before/after recorded; a mis-numbered citation is corrected.
5. **Un-annotated amendment defects** — the missing annotation is added, with the before/after recorded.
6. **Nothing else.** A repair that would alter a score, a rank, a hard-stop flag, a gap's status, a rejection's
   verdict, a candidate's status, a **map row**, or the **content** of a baseline row's substantive claim is
   **not** a repair and is **not** made. **No row may be deleted or renumbered.**

### Cycle 136 — Priority 1 — the nine blind probes, batch 1 (rows A–I). WRITTEN BEFORE THE BATCH'S CLOSING ENTRIES WERE READ.

**Status of this block.** These nine probes were written **blind**, under the rule fixed in the pre-registration
above, and were **fixed in this file** before `R-039 … R-046` (the batch's closing entries) and the batch's
known-baseline rows 68 … 75 were read. Each probe is written with the register's four fields — **state**,
**flow**, **sign claim**, **instance** — and with an explicit statement of **the one feature that differs from the
row's own kind**, which is what makes it a near-miss rather than a restatement of the kind.

**One recorded leak, disclosed.** While locating the known-baseline table for Priority 2's pre-registration, the
probe writer's own search printed **baseline row 68** — template **A**'s own baseline row, including its four
recorded reasons — in full. The leak therefore touches **probe A only**, and **probe A's blind status is
qualified**: it is written from the map label and from the method, but the writer has seen row A's baseline text.
This is recorded here, before the screens are run, so that the qualification is part of the record rather than an
afterthought; probes B … I are blind without qualification.

---

**Probe A — row A: "The price of a funding, balance-sheet or capacity constraint" (repo specialness, lending fee
curves, CDS financing spreads, standing-repo award rates).**

- **The near-miss state kind, named:** the published **cross-sectional dispersion** of a constraint's price — a
  published table quoting **one** constraint's price across **named participant tiers**, from which the price's
  *cross-section* (and each tier's position within it) is public at decision time.
- **The one feature that differs from row A's own kind:** row A's kind is the **level** of a constraint price, a
  single series; the probe's kind is the **cross-section of the same price**, a different published object whose
  content is **relative** — which tier pays more than which — rather than absolute.
- **State:** a published, decision-time cross-section of one funding-constraint price across named borrower tiers
  (for example a securities-lending fee curve quoted by borrower tier, or a published cross-section of CDS
  financing spreads by counterparty), from which each participant's own price and the cross-sectional dispersion
  are computable.
- **Flow:** the participant's own funding transaction, priced at its own tier's quoted rate.
- **Sign claim:** the *sign* of the tier's cost disadvantage is read off the published cross-section itself — the
  top tier pays more than the median tier — so the published state determines a **direction** of relative cost,
  not a size; and a third party who can fund the cheap tier and retire the expensive tier's exposure harvests a
  concession whose **sign** is fixed by the published dispersion rather than by its level.
- **Instance:** a daily published securities-lending fee curve quoted by borrower tier, or a published
  cross-section of CDS financing spreads by counterparty.

**Probe B — row B: "Pair-level netted positions (a convergence crowd)".**

- **The near-miss state kind, named:** a **published aggregate that bounds** the pair-level netted position — two
  published market-wide aggregates, one per leg, from which the pair's netted identity is **bounded but not
  computed**.
- **The one feature that differs from row B's own kind:** row B's kind is the **exact pair-level netted identity**
  (which the structural null says is not constructible from published data); the probe's kind is a **published
  aggregate that brackets it** — a coarser, public object that is *not* the identity.
- **State:** published market-wide aggregate position statistics for each leg of a convergence pair (for example a
  venue's published open interest for one leg and a regulator's published aggregate position statistic for the
  other), from which the pair's netted position can be **bounded**.
- **Flow:** the convergence crowd's own liquidation of one leg when the pair's price relationship breaks.
- **Sign claim:** the published aggregates determine **which leg the crowd must liquidate** — the leg whose
  published aggregate exceeds the other's by more than the pair's own scale — and therefore the **sign** of the
  pressure on each leg; the state decides a direction, not a size.
- **Instance:** a published aggregate open-interest or aggregate-position series for two related futures markets.

**Probe C — row C: "A published fee or toll that prices a third party's dated flow".**

- **The near-miss state kind, named:** a published **rebate or liquidity concession** — a **negative** fee paid by
  a venue to the counterparty whose trade **offsets** a dated third-party flow — with the schedule published
  **across venues**, so the published object is a **relative** schedule rather than a single toll.
- **The one feature that differs from row C's own kind:** row C's kind is a **charge levied on** the dated flow;
  the probe's kind is a **payment made for absorbing** it, and the state is a **cross-venue differential**.
- **State:** a venue's published rebate or concession schedule for liquidity provision, differentiated by side,
  and the corresponding published schedule of at least one competing venue.
- **Flow:** the third party's dated flow.
- **Sign claim:** if the published rebate differential between two venues exceeds the cost of routing the
  offsetting trade, then the **sign** of the arbitrage is fixed by which venue pays more; the published schedule
  determines the direction of the concession, not its size.
- **Instance:** a published exchange maker/taker rebate schedule and a competitor's published equivalent.

**Probe D — row D: "A published count or queue".**

- **The near-miss state kind, named:** a **signed** published count — a published count of one kind of pending
  item **net of** the opposite kind (net new orders less cancellations; a published count of pending *buy*
  interest net of pending *sell* interest), so that the **sign** is carried by the number itself.
- **The one feature that differs from row D's own kind:** row D's kind is a count as a **level** (a magnitude of
  pending items); the probe's kind is a count as a **signed quantity** whose zero-crossing is the state.
- **State:** a published, continuously updated **signed** pending-item count — the net of two opposite kinds of
  pending item — public at decision time.
- **Flow:** the flow that must absorb the imbalance when the signed count crosses zero.
- **Sign claim:** the **sign of the imbalance** is read off the published number itself rather than inferred from
  its level, so the state determines a **direction**; the price effect of the absorbing flow follows from the
  imbalance's sign.
- **Instance:** a published net order-flow or net pending-interest count from a venue or a regulator.

**Probe E — row E: "A published reserve, availability or headroom".**

- **The near-miss state kind, named:** the **absorber's** published capacity — a published reserve, availability or
  headroom figure belonging to the party that would **take the other side** of the flow, published by a third
  party at decision time — rather than the rationed party's own headroom.
- **The one feature that differs from row E's own kind:** row E's kind is the constrained party's **own** published
  headroom; the probe's kind is the **counterparty-side** capacity, whose sign-content is about the *absence* of
  a concession rather than about the rationing of the flow's own obligor.
- **State:** a published, decision-time figure of the **absorbing** capacity available against a dated flow — a
  published aggregate of the collateral or credit a central counterparty or a depository holds against the member
  that will take the other side.
- **Flow:** the dated third-party flow.
- **Sign claim:** whether the dated flow has a price impact **at all** is determined by comparing the published
  absorbing capacity with the published size of the flow; the comparison flips the **existence** of the effect and,
  where it exists, its sign.
- **Instance:** a central counterparty's published daily margin or collateral figure, or a central securities
  depository's published settlement-liquidity statistic.

**Probe F — row F: "A published constraint breach / non-compliance event".**

- **The near-miss state kind, named:** the published breach **together with its published remedy** — a published,
  dated determination that states a **quantified, named** obligation transferring a sum from one named party to
  another.
- **The one feature that differs from row F's own kind:** row F's kind is the **breach event**; the probe's kind is
  the breach **plus its remedy**, whose content is a dated transfer of a stated amount between two named parties —
  an object a breach record alone does not carry.
- **State:** a published, dated enforcement, arbitral or restorative determination that states a make-whole sum
  and names the obliged payer and the beneficiary.
- **Flow:** the obliged payer's dated payment.
- **Sign claim:** the sign of the price effect of the payment is determined by the published determination (the payer
  must raise funds by buying or selling to make the payment), so the state determines a **direction**; and the
  determination is published and dated, so the state is decision-time.
- **Instance:** a published restitution or make-whole determination naming a sum, a payer and a beneficiary.

**Probe G — row G: "A published waiver or amendment event".**

- **The near-miss state kind, named:** the **lapse** of a relief — the published expiry or non-renewal of a
  previously granted waiver or exemption — so that the event is the **return to the constraint** rather than the
  grant of relief.
- **The one feature that differs from row G's own kind:** row G's kind is relief **arriving** (a grant or an
  amendment); the probe's kind is relief **leaving** (a lapse), which forces a flow in the **opposite** direction to
  the grant case.
- **State:** a published register of exemptions, waivers or relief instruments, each carrying a stated expiry date,
  and the expiry of the entries currently in it.
- **Flow:** the flow that returns when the relief lapses — the party must again buy or sell the constrained thing.
- **Sign claim:** a lapsing relief to sell forces a returning **buyer**, so the sign of the price effect is fixed by
  the published expiry and is the mirror of the grant case; the expiry is published and dated, so the state is
  decision-time.
- **Instance:** a published exemption register with stated expiry dates.

**Probe H — row H: "A published regulatory change of law".**

- **The near-miss state kind, named:** a published **adjudicated** change in legal status — a dated judgment or
  determination that **classifies** a named instrument or class of instruments as subject to, or exempt from, a
  published regime from a stated date.
- **The one feature that differs from row H's own kind:** row H's kind is a change in the **rule** made by a
  rulemaker; the probe's kind is a change in the **legal status of a named instrument or class**, produced by an
  adjudication rather than by an amendment.
- **State:** a published, dated adjudication or determination classifying a named instrument or class of
  instruments as subject to (or exempt from) a published regime from a stated date.
- **Flow:** the mandatory flow that the classification triggers, or ceases to trigger.
- **Sign claim:** the sign of the flow's price effect is determined by the determination's **content** — whether
  the classification imposes a mandatory purchase or a mandatory surrender — and the determination is published and
  dated, so the state is decision-time and unanticipated.
- **Instance:** a published court or agency ruling reclassifying a contract or a security from a stated date.

**Probe I — row I: "A published clamp or cap band on a continuously published state".**

- **The near-miss state kind, named:** a **temporary** clamp — a published band imposed with a **published sunset
  date** (and, where the sunset is conditional, the published condition and its published status).
- **The one feature that differs from row I's own kind:** row I's kind is a **standing** band on a continuously
  published state; the probe's kind is a band whose **own publication carries its end date**, so the state includes
  the band *and* its termination, and the content that matters is the **release** at the sunset rather than the
  binding.
- **State:** a published, dated **temporary** cap or band on a continuously published state, with the sunset date
  stated in the same publication.
- **Flow:** the participation the clamp held back, returning at the sunset.
- **Sign claim:** a published band and its published sunset determine the **direction** of the released
  participation — a cap on participation above a price holds back buying at high prices, and its removal releases
  buying — so the published band-and-sunset state determines the sign of the release rather than its size.
- **Instance:** a published temporary position limit or emergency measure with a stated expiry.

**The batch as fixed, in the order the probes were written:** A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I. Nine probes, one per row,
none yet screened. **Zero fetches** have been made and **no literature has been consulted**; the closing entries
`R-039 … R-046` and the baseline rows 68 … 75 had not been read when this block was written.

## Cycle 137 — 2026-10-22 — pre-registration (written BEFORE the cycle's first artifact write beyond this block, and BEFORE the first probe was written)

Cycle 137 executes the Cycle-136 handoff's three priorities. This block is the pre-registration. The batch of
probes, the blind-writing rule, the outcome categories, the decision on the Cycle-136 membership-test proposal and
the stated expectation are fixed here for Priority 1; the two handed-off audit findings and the repair list are
fixed here for Priority 2; and the gap tracking and the housekeeping list are fixed here for Priority 3 — so that
neither a verdict, a repair nor a count can be re-written after the fact.

### Three-pass task-framing loop

**Pass 1 — Draft.** Objective: **(Priority 1)** *execute* clause X-1, the near-miss probe of the register's own
coverage map, in **batches 2, 3 and 4** — the twenty-four rows **10 … 33** less the rows already closed in full —
writing each probe blind and screening it under the **unchanged** narrowed rule; **(Priority 2)** decide the two
findings the Cycle-136 baseline audit handed forward — whether **R-065's closed kind** gets a coverage-map row of
its own, and what the **R-048** correspondence in map row 17's "Closed by" cell means — and repair either in place
with a before/after; **(Priority 3)** track the open gaps (**no action on G-37, no action on G-33**) and run
housekeeping. Scope boundary: theory only; **zero fetches** unless and until a probe survives the screens and the
narrowed rule's own literature step is reached (it is not expected to be); no market-data acquisition or processing;
no computation of any strategy statistic; no backtest, simulation, parameter sweep or significance test; no strategy
or signal implementation; no executable research infrastructure; no job or workflow launch; no change to the
canonical prompt; no trading.

**Pass 2 — Critique.** (i) *A probe that is written after the kill it tests is a tautology.* The blind-writing rule
is fixed **in this block, before the first probe is written**, and — **a strengthening of the Cycle-136 rule,
registered here in advance** — **all twenty-two probes of the three batches are fixed in this file before *any* of
the twenty-two rows' closing entries is read**, not merely before the closing entries of the batch the probe
belongs to. The per-batch rule of Cycle 136 is therefore not the rule used here; the stricter rule is, and the
difference is recorded rather than glossed. (ii) *A probe must not become a re-run of a route the register has
already closed.* X-1 reads **no document**, consults **no literature**, and is not the forward route (constructions
from the register's free memory), not the backward route (447 of 447, exhausted) and not the Cycle-132
literature-first route amendment (rejected, and **not** re-opened). Its **source of constructions is the map's own
rows**. (iii) *A probe must not be a rediscovery.* If a probe reproduces a construction the register has already
screened (R-063 … R-069, or the Cycles 115–121 state-kind screens), the outcome category is **REDISCOVERY**,
recorded as such and **not** counted as a new kill. (iv) *A kill must name its clause.* A probe that dies dies **by
a named clause or template or recorded structural result**, and a probe that cannot name one **is not killed** — it
is recorded as **UNDECIDED** and handed off, because the register's own principle ("a kill which cannot name a
clause is not a kill") cuts both ways. (v) *The expectation must be stated before the result and must not
substitute for the screen.* The expectation is recorded below and the screen is run regardless of it. (vi) *A probe
must not be written to fit a general clause.* Each probe below is written **first**, and its screen is run
**second**; the pre-registered expectation of twenty-two kills is therefore not a licence to write twenty-two
tautologies, and the finding that the membership argument carried **9 of 9** in batch 1 is a *hypothesis about the
template programme*, not a licence to skip the clause screens. (vii) *The audit must not become a licence.* A
repair that changes a substantive claim is not a repair, and is not made.

**Pass 3 — Revise and red-team (the task as executed).** Record: the twenty-two probes as written blind; the
twenty-two screens with their named clause or template; the batch-by-batch outcome tally; the map and baseline
edits the batches require; the two Priority-2 findings with their decisions and their before/afters; the open gaps
tracked; the counts re-derived **from the files**; the rubric arithmetic re-run **from the shortlist's own cells**;
all five artifact headers and their newest dated blocks advanced to "Cycle 137 complete" and **read back in this
session**; the standing identifier-integrity check run. Every external claim points to an `S-` entry. **No `IDEA-`
identifier may be consumed unless a probe survives every screen *and* then passes the narrowed rule's own
literature step.**

### Priority 1 — clause X-1, the near-miss probe, **batches 2–4: coverage-map rows 10 … 33 less the rows already closed in full**. REGISTERED BEFORE THE FIRST PROBE WAS WRITTEN.

**The instrument.** The register's own artifacts: the coverage map (33 rows at the start of this cycle), the narrowed
rule (R-063's, unchanged since Cycle 117), the strict bar, the Cycle-52 third test, G-12, G-13, the nine templates,
the known-baseline table and the rejection log. **The probe reads no document and consults no literature. Zero
fetches** unless a probe survives and the rule's own literature step is then reached.

**The batch, fixed in advance: rows 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 (batch 2) · 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25
(batch 3) · 26, 28, 31, 32, 33 (batch 4).** The batch boundary is the one X-1 itself pre-registered in Cycle 135
(**"Rows are taken in pre-registered batches: A–I (the template programme), 10–17, 18–25, 26–33"**), and it is
**not** re-chosen here. **Three rows are excluded from the twenty-four, by a rule fixed in this block, before any
probe was written:** **row 27** (closed in full in Cycle 128 by R-068 D4's count-dilemma), **row 29** (closed in full
in Cycle 136 by probe D) and **row 30** (closed in full in Cycle 136 by probe E). The rule is: **a row that is
already closed *in full* has no residual for X-1 to probe**, because X-1's target is the nearest state kind that
the row's own closing clause does **not** cover, and a row closed in full has no such kind left. The exclusion is a
consequence of the method, not a choice made after seeing a result, and it is recorded as a deviation from the
handoff's "rows 10–33" phrasing, whose intent (the pre-registered batches) is preserved exactly.
**At most one probe per row.** **Twenty-two probes, in three batches, all fixed in this file before any closing
entry is read.**

**The blind-writing rule, fixed in advance.** For each row, the probe is written from **the row's map label alone** —
the "Published state kind" cell, with its parenthetical examples where the map gives them — together with the
register's own method (the narrowed rule, the strict bar, G-12, G-13, the Cycle-52 third test, the obligor's-own-flow
clause, the aggregated-obligor side, the count-dilemma, and the nine templates as *labels*). The row's **closing
rejection entry** and the row's **known-baseline row** are **not read** until **all twenty-two probes are written and
fixed in this file**. Each probe is written with the register's four fields — **state**, **flow**, **sign claim**,
**instance** — and with an explicit statement of **the one feature that differs from the row's own kind**, which is
what makes it a *near-miss* rather than a restatement of the kind.

**The four outcome categories, fixed in advance.** Unchanged from Cycle 136.

1. **KILL — named clause or template.** The probe is killed by a **named** clause (the accounting-by-product
   clause, rule (i); the obligor's-own-flow clause; the sign-versus-magnitude clause, **G-12**; the
   publication-before-the-decision clause, **G-13**; the published-baseline clause, rule (ii); the anticipation and
   competition clause; the Cycle-52 third test; the strict bar's decision-time, sign-determining, unclaimed-sign and
   feasible-clean-test limbs) or by a **named template** (A–I) or by a **named structural result already recorded**
   (for example the **count-dilemma**, R-068 D4, or the **aggregated-obligor side**, R-067). The kill is written into
   the map row and the known-baseline table with the clause named.
2. **SURVIVOR.** The probe satisfies **every** clause of the narrowed rule. **There is no partial survivor.** A
   survivor is a **construction**, not a candidate: the narrowed rule's **own** literature step must then be run on
   it (and only then may it become a candidate). **This is the only circumstance in which this method spends a
   fetch**, and it is not expected to be reached.
3. **REDISCOVERY.** The probe reproduces a construction the register has already screened. It is recorded as
   rediscovery, it is **not** counted as a new kill, and the batch's selection is faulted.
4. **UNDECIDED.** The screen cannot return a verdict without a fetch that the rule does not license at this point.
   It is **recorded and handed off**, never dropped.

**The decision on the Cycle-136 membership-test proposal. REGISTERED BEFORE THE FIRST PROBE.** Cycle 136 recorded
an *observation*, not a clause: the **membership** argument — *the probe's state kind is a member of the row's own
kind* — carried **nine of nine** kills, and a membership test "would have killed nine of nine probes at zero cost
and before any clause was applied". The Cycle-136 handoff carried it to this cycle "as a proposal for the next
batch's pre-registration, not an adopted clause". **Decision, fixed here in advance: the membership test is adopted
as the screen's *first step* — a triage that orders and records the screen — and is NOT adopted as a kill.** The
reason is the register's own standard, which cuts against the proposal: a kill must **name a clause or template**,
and "the probe's kind is a member of the row's own kind" names no clause at all; it is a *description* of the probe,
and a description cannot kill. If membership were a kill, the register's screens would become decorative, and
Cycle 136's own nine kills would have been nine tautologies rather than nine applications of the templates'
recorded reasons. **Every kill recorded in this cycle therefore names a clause or a template or a recorded
structural result**, and the membership verdict is recorded alongside it as corroboration. The proposal is
**resolved**, not deferred.

**The stated expectation, fixed in advance and not permitted to substitute for the screen: twenty-two kills.** The
reason is the register's own: a sub-variant of a kind is usually covered by the clause that closed the kind (9 of 9
in batch 1), and the register's **entire** prior evidence on X-1 is one probe in one row — R-067's carried-forward
residual → R-068's D4 → the count-dilemma → **row 27 closed in full** — which produced a kill. **A survivor is
possible** and would be the register's **first in forty-six named constructions** and would open the narrowed rule's
own exit. **Either outcome is a gain**: a kill closes a row **in full** rather than by kind; a survivor is the only
thing that can open the exit. **Twenty-two kills is the expectation, not the result.**

**What this priority may consume.** An **`R-` identifier** (one new rejection entry recording the batches' kills, the
first free identifier being **R-070**), and **baseline rows**. **The baseline rule, fixed in advance:** for each
killed probe, the killed kind is a **member of its map row's own kind** (this is the design of X-1 and it is the
membership verdict of the first step). The baseline row that **guards** that kind is **amended in place** with the
probe's named kill, following R-068 D4's precedent exactly — a new guard row would assert a novelty the kill does
not have. **If no existing row guards the killed kind, a new baseline row is written** (numbered from **112**) **and
the map row's citation cell is amended to cite it**; where the guarding row exists but the map row does not cite it,
the map row's citation cell is amended to cite it, and the amendment is recorded. **No baseline row is deleted,
renumbered or reordered. The map's row count is not changed by this priority** (the one map row this cycle adds is a
Priority-2 decision, registered there). An **`IDEA-` identifier only if** a probe survives every screen **and** then
passes the rule's own literature step. **No `S-` identifier** unless that literature step is reached. **No `G-`
identifier** is opened, because every kill is expected to be structural and independent of data availability.

### Priority 2 — the two findings handed off from the Cycle-136 baseline audit. REGISTERED BEFORE THE FIRST REPAIR.

**Finding (i) — R-065's closed kind has no coverage-map row, and its guard row (99) is cited by no map row.** The
handoff asks this cycle to *decide whether to add a map row*, and to record a before/after. **Decision rule, fixed
in advance:** the map's stated subject is *the register's published-state-kind space, as it now stands* — an
enumeration of the state kinds the register has **closed**. R-065's kind ("a dated, published supply-loss notice") is
a closed state kind: it was closed by a screen, it has a guard row (**99**), and it is a published state kind in the
register's own sense. A closed kind that has no map row is a **hole in the enumeration**, and the map's claim to
enumerate the register's closed state kinds is false while the hole stands. **The default decision is therefore to
ADD the map row**, with the guard row's number cited and R-065 named as the closing entry, and to record the
before/after. **One consequence is registered here, before the repair, so that it cannot be discovered after the
fact:** the added row is **not probed** under X-1 in this cycle, because the Priority-1 batch is fixed above and
adding a probe to it after the fact would be the same fault X-1 exists to prevent. The added row is therefore
**handed to Cycle 138 as the single unprobed row**, and the handover says so. **The repair list for this finding is
fixed in advance as:** (a) the new map row, in the map's own positional convention, at the end of the table, with
its number, its state kind, its closing entry and its guard row; (b) the map's row-count statements corrected
**everywhere they appear in the artifact set**, with each correction recorded; (c) the Cycle-136 note above the
known-baseline table — which lists the rows "not represented in the map" — corrected so that row **99** leaves that

### Cycle 137 — Priority 1 — the twenty-one blind probes, batches 2–4 (rows 10 … 33 less the three rows closed in full). WRITTEN BEFORE ANY OF THE TWENTY-ONE ROWS' CLOSING ENTRIES WAS READ.

**Correction to this block's own heading and its closing line (see the correction note above).** The heading and the

**Status of this block.** These twenty-two probes were written **blind**, under the rule fixed in the

or their known-baseline rows was read**. This is **stricter** than Cycle 136's per-batch rule, and the difference is

**Leaks, disclosed.** (i) The **coverage map itself** was read before the probes were written — necessarily, since
